issues.description: Check contract is inconsistent: metadata/PR promise PASS/FAIL but code emits a third MANUAL state for GKE.
issues.detail: PR title and metadata.json document a two-valued postcondition (PASS=single, FAIL=multiple), but the implementation introduces MANUAL for gke-* instances. Either document MANUAL in metadata and PR description, or drop the GKE carve-out. The spec and code must agree.

issues.description: GKE detection by `name.startswith('gke-')` is a fragile string-sniff where an authoritative signal exists.
issues.detail: Users can name any VM gke-* and earn a free MANUAL pass. The authoritative signals are the `goog-gke-node` label or the managed-instance-group reference. Add an `is_gke_managed` boolean to the Instance ADT derived from labels/MIG in the service, and key the exemption off that.

issues.description: Naming drifts between 'single' and 'multiple' across PR title, CheckID, directory, and CHANGELOG.
issues.detail: PR title and CHANGELOG describe 'multiple network interfaces' detection while the directory, files, class, and CheckID all use 'single_network_interface'. Pick one predicate and align CheckID, paths, class name, and changelog so future grep and docs stay coherent.

issues.description: Zero-NIC branch silently PASSes with no test, violating the 'single interface' postcondition.
issues.detail: When `interface_count == 0` the code falls through to PASS with an informational message. A VM with zero NICs is not 'single network interface'; it is degenerate. Either treat it as MANUAL/INFO explicitly, or assert it cannot occur per the GCP API. Add test coverage either way.

issues.description: Mutable default `network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = []` on Instance model.
issues.detail: Pydantic v1 copies the default safely, but the idiomatic and contract-preserving form is `Field(default_factory=list)`. Match the surrounding codebase style and state the per-instance ownership invariant explicitly to avoid future aliasing surprises.

issues.description: Redundant `public_ip` loop on Instance instead of deriving from NetworkInterface.
issues.detail: The new NetworkInterface struct only stores name/network/subnetwork while `public_ip` is still computed by a parallel loop on Instance. Fold accessConfigs/natIP into NetworkInterface and derive `public_ip` via `any(nic.public_ip for nic in instance.network_interfaces)`. One pass, one source of truth.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the check works and is tested, but ships with a contract mismatch and a taste-grade flaw that a maintainer would bounce. PR title, metadata, CheckID, and CHANGELOG disagree on whether the predicate is 'single' or 'multiple' and whether MANUAL is a valid outcome. GKE detection by `name.startswith('gke-')` is special-casing where an authoritative signal (goog-gke-node label or MIG reference) exists. The zero-NIC branch silently PASSes with no test. Smaller cleanups: switch to `default_factory=list` for the new list field and fold `public_ip` into the new NetworkInterface struct so there is one source of truth.
